summary.headline: Whirlpool of India Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR 2,181 crore, but PBT margin fell to 5% on e-waste and energy-change costs.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew high single digits to INR 2,181 crore, helped by washers, air conditioners (up about 50%) and Elica (up 30%), with March 2026 the highest shipment month in company history. Profit fell sharply: EBITDA was INR 121 crore (5.6%, down 33.7%) and profit before exceptional items INR 110 crore (5%, down 29%), mainly from incremental e-waste provisions and unrecovered BEE energy-upgrade costs. Refrigerator market share fell triple digits in direct cool and frost free due to the January 2026 energy-regulation phase-in/phase-out and deliberate non-matching of competitor pricing. For FY26, revenue rose 1.4% to INR 8,034 crore, EBITDA was INR 481 crore (6%), and reported PBT fell 19% including a INR 38.8 crore one-time wage code charge. Management gave no margin guidance and flagged FY27 as a difficult year.

segments.name: Refrigerators
segments.commentary: Industry declined in refrigerators for FY26, led by direct cool; company direct cool and frost free volume share fell triple digits in Jan-Mar 2026 due to the energy-regulation changeover and competitive pricing. Management expects share recovery as phase-in completes in April-June.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Gaining share: front load volumes doubled in Q4 with triple-digit share gains; top load strong double-digit gains with a number two position in Q4 (multi-brand outlet volume); semi-automatic number two, with Dynamix technology now nearly half of that business.

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Crossed 100,000 units in March 2026; Q4 growth above 50%, FY26 growth above 40%. ASP roughly 2x core products, and working capital is heavier, with a planned AC inventory and receivables build lifting Q4 networking capital.

segments.name: Elica (kitchen appliances)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 30% (32% per CFO) and PBT up 48%; FY26 revenue up 12% and profit up 15%. Management wants to keep margins in the double digits.

guidance_outlook: No margin guidance given; management called FY27 difficult for the industry and the company due to energy changes, e-waste provisions, competitive pricing and the Middle East war.
Long-term ambition: high single-digit margins for refrigerator, washing machine and AC business; revenue growth ambition moved to early double digits.
Large-capacity frost free refrigerator launch planned for Q2 FY27, filling a portfolio gap.
Energy-upgrade cost described as permanent; next energy change expected in about three years.
Management expects continued aggressive investment over the next 12 to 24 months in innovation, automation, cost capex, and possible backward integration or adjacency M&A.
No buyback under consideration at this point; cash to be deployed in organic or inorganic growth.
capex_capacity: CWIP of about INR 200 crore relates to the premium frost free refrigerator capacity, expected to be capitalised after the Q2 FY27 launch.
AC manufacturing is currently outsourced to 3PL partners; management will decide on own-plant capex based on economics and depreciation impact, and says it is not yet committed.
Automation across factories and cost-saving capex (factory, product, network) under evaluation, traded off against payback.
Quality ratings: Pune at Silver, Puducherry and Faridabad at Bronze, with a target of Silver for both.
Management says it has no budget constraints and is evaluating inorganic options of similar size to Elica.
demand_pricing: Industry grew low single digits in Jan-Mar 2026 and was roughly flat for FY26; refrigerator industry declined for the year, led by direct cool.
Competitive pricing remained very aggressive; the company chose not to match it fully, which cost volume share.
Energy upcharge of the BEE upgrade was not recovered through pricing as of March 31, 2026; management says it is theoretically recoverable by price but depends on competitor behaviour.
Management flagged Middle East war impacts on oil-linked inputs, imported components (20-35% of components for industry players) and forex.

In March 2026 the company reached number two in refrigerator plus washing machine volume share in multi-brand outlets (for one month); it was number one in direct cool for four months from December 2025.

qa_highlights.question: What were the e-waste and energy-upcharge costs for Q4 and FY26, and will they recur in FY27? Is channel inventory normalising to allow recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the split. E-waste is provided at the highest rate under discussion with the ministry and recyclers; any rationalisation would be a benefit. The energy upcharge is a permanent BOM cost increase, and the next energy change is about three years away.

qa_highlights.question: What scenarios could play out with raw material, freight and regulatory cost increases: competitive rationalisation or consumer downtrading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said anything could happen and called it a roll of the dice. It is focused on component supply through the Strait of Hormuz, forex (imported content 20-35%) and pricing, and it will protect volume if it is materially outpriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 AC revenue contribution, the aspiration, and the capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: AC revenue is not disclosed; refrigerators are over 50% of revenue and washers 25-30%. The AC aim is strong but responsible growth, offtake-led, with no aspiration to be number one in AC for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and is a buyback planned?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said cash will go to innovation, automation, cost capex, backward integration and possible inorganic deals; there is no dividend or buyback plan at present. Management said buyback has not been looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the three-to-five-year strategy, and why not a buyback despite the stock price?
qa_highlights.answer: The vision is to become the number one in refrigerators and washing machines in under 10 years, probably more than five. Management said it is focused on the next 12 to 24 months of investment and said executives bought shares personally.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the refrigerator industry stayed flat, and could BEE ratings help demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a K-curve with the entry segment (direct cool and semi-automatic) lagging. Replacement demand is being postponed. It said higher star ratings raise cost and price, so the effect on demand is complex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin outlook for Elica and the rest of the business, and what adjacency is being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Long term, high single-digit margins are likely for refrigerator, washing machine and AC businesses; Elica is held in double digits and its penetration is below 5%. Adjacencies must be synergistic on go-to-market and profitable, not low-margin.

risks_watch: Unrecovered energy-upgrade and e-waste costs: margins could stay pressured if pricing does not catch up in April-June 2026 and beyond.
Whether refrigerator share recovers as the phase-in/phase-out completes and the new frost free large-capacity launch lands in Q2 FY27.
Competitive pricing intensity in refrigerators and washers and the volume-versus-margin trade-off.
Middle East war impacts on component supply, freight, oil-linked inputs and forex.
Working capital build from AC inventory and receivables; management expects it to reverse in the next quarter.
Capital allocation: no buyback, with M&A and capex under evaluation over the next 12 to 24 months; no timeline given.
Pending e-waste policy rationalisation between the ministry, producers and recyclers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term vision and the share gains in washers and AC, but cautious and non-committal on FY27 margins, pricing and buybacks. Management declined to quantify the regulatory costs and avoided discussing April-May pricing.

And so you can see that without the air conditioner mix impact, our gross margin would have continued to grow.
Margins, to be honest, we can't give any guidance right now.
So, we would like to be the best in refrigerators and washing machines.
So, buyback is something that we've not looked at, at this point in time because we think there is lot of opportunity that we can actually take.

adds.what: Premium large-capacity frost free refrigerator capacity (CWIP ~INR 200 crore), launch planned Q2 FY27
Air conditioner own-plant capacity under evaluation; AC currently outsourced to 3PL partners, not yet committed

growth.why: No near-term revenue guidance; management called FY27 difficult and gave no margin guidance, with growth tied to a Q2 FY27 frost-free launch, share recovery as the energy changeover completes, and a long-term early double-digit revenue CAGR ambition that lacks specific orders or capacity numbers.
